passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael Wayne Short was born. He grew up with three siblings, one brother and two sisters.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael Short did not finish high school.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: He married his first wife at age 17.
bold: married his first wife at age 17

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael went through three divorces.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael’s uncle, Frank Arrington, described Michael as having a rough-and-tumble childhood and said Michael was not pampered growing up.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Mary Frances Hall was born.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Mary Hall grew up on a tobacco farm in Franklin County, Virginia.
bold: tobacco farm in Franklin County, Virginia

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: According to her brother Carloyn Hodges, Mary was the most outgoing of the family’s three children, although she was generally quiet around people she did not know.
bold: most outgoing of the family’s three children

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Hodges said Mary was “rarely outgoing” around strangers but enjoyed talking and spending time with people she knew.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: By the mid-1980s, Michael had met Mary Hall in Rocky Mount, Virginia, at a bar called The Blue Jeans.
bold: Mary Hall in Rocky Mount, Virginia

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael and Mary met and began a relationship. The couple later married and settled in Henry County, Virginia.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Ronnie Ray described Michael as a good worker.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Ray said that after Jennifer was born, Michael often talked about her proudly.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: 1990s: Michael drove a truck for Rocky Mount Ready Mix for about five years.
bold: Rocky Mount Ready Mix for about five years

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Mary Short worked at the Pluma Inc. plant in the Bowles Industrial Park. Coworkers reportedly knew her as “Little Mary.”
bold: Pluma Inc. plant in the Bowles Industrial Park

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: During this period, Mary reportedly experienced unwanted attention from an unidentified man who came to the plant looking for her on multiple occasions.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: In one reported 1992 incident, the man entered the plant and a manager ordered him to leave. He reportedly left in a white pickup truck.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The encounters later became important to investigators following Mary’s murder. In August 2002, police received information about a possible former stalker, and investigators released older photographs of Mary while trying to identify the man.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael and Mary welcomed their daughter, Jennifer Renee Short.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer was Michael’s fourth child, and the only child Michael and Mary had together.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: M.S. Mobile Home Movers Inc. Established: Michael operated a mobile-home moving business known as M.S. Mobile Home Movers Inc.
bold: M.S. Mobile Home Movers Inc. Established:

passages.text: MS Mobile Home Movers Inc. held a license #2705040949 with the Virginia Contractors License Board, expiring on 08-31-2003.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Family Friend Visits the Shorts: Family friend Sheila Davis stopped by the Short residence to drop off payment for work Michael had completed. Davis recalled that what was intended to be a brief 15-minute visit turned into approximately an hour of conversation with the family.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Davis later described Michael and Mary as hardworking, close to Jennifer and devoted to spending time together as a family.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Mary regularly helped Michael with his mobile-home moving work, including unloading cinder blocks.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael and Mary rarely used a babysitter because, according to Davis, they preferred spending their free time with Jennifer.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Short Family Planned Move to Callaway: Michael and Mary Short were planning to move back to Callaway, Virginia, where Mary had grown up.
bold: Short Family Planned Move to Callaway:

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael and Mary Short operated M.S. Mobile Home Movers, a business that moved mobile homes.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Short family was considering relocating to South Carolina. As part of that possibility, Michael traveled to areas of South Carolina seeking employment.

passages.text: Bennettsville, South Carolina

passages.text: Florence, South Carolina

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer completed third grade.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: She spent considerable time with her parents and frequently accompanied Michael on nonschool days while he worked.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer turned 9 on July 12, 2002.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Her parents bought school supplies and children’s clothing to prepare for the upcoming school year.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer celebrated her 9th birthday.

passages.text: Jennifer was enrolled to return to Figsboro Elementary School for fourth grade.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities continue to seek anyone who had contact with Michael, Mary or Jennifer Short between August 1 and August 14, 2002.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: They also want information from anyone whose mobile home Michael’s company moved during 2002 and who investigators have never interviewed.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael continued making trips to South Carolina while the family considered relocating.

passages.text: Michael and Mary took a concrete step toward leaving their Henry County home.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Shorts contacted real estate agent Marlene Dalton and asked her to put their house up for sale.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael reportedly explained that his business was slow and that the family had a mobile home where they could live temporarily.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: An open house was scheduled for Sunday, August 18, 2002, three days after Michael and Mary were found murdered and Jennifer disappeared.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Ray remembered Jennifer proudly showing him her third-grade report card and said she was “smiling and grinning.”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael was already talking about Jennifer beginning school soon and how well she had done in third grade.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer Seen at Concrete Business: Former Short employee Ronnie Ray, owner of Rocky Mount Ready Mix, said he last saw Jennifer when Michael brought her with him to Ray’s concrete business on August 12, three days before the murders.

passages.text: 11:13 p.m. – Circle C Convenience Store: Surveillance footage captured Jennifer Short inside the Circle C convenience store near her family’s home. The footage was recorded less than two days before Michael and Mary Short were discovered murdered, and Jennifer was reported missing.
bold: Jennifer Short inside the Circle C convenience store

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The surveillance image provides one of the final known visual records of Jennifer before her disappearance.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Thompson stayed at a motel near the Short residence and returned after leaving Michael that evening.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Thompson told investigators that Michael, Mary and Jennifer were alive when he left the residence. Later accounts state that Jennifer had already gone to bed. Thompson would become one of the last known people to see the family before the murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Thompson and Michael had plans for the following morning. They were supposed to travel to Christiansburg, Virginia, to pick up a truck for Michael’s mobile-home moving business.

The receipt provides a documented transaction from the family’s final evening before Michael and Mary Short were murdered and Jennifer Short was abducted.

passages.text: The Short family spent what would become their final evening at their Oak Level home.

passages.text: Investigators believe the murders and Jennifer’s abduction occurred sometime between midnight on August 14 and approximately 9:00 a.m. on August 15, 2002.

passages.text: At some point during the overnight or early morning hours, the person or persons responsible entered or gained access to the Short residence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: An unidentified man was reportedly seen parked along U.S. Highway 220 near the Short home during the early morning hours. Investigators later sought to identify the man and the vehicle associated with the sighting.

passages.text: Wayne Davis, then a Henry County patrol deputy and now sheriff, was among the first officers to respond.

passages.text: Deputies found Michael Short on a couch in the attached garage area of the residence. He had been shot once in the head.

passages.text: Later reporting concerning the crime scene described Mary’s mattress as having been displaced by approximately two inches and her pillow as being on the bedroom floor.

passages.text: There was no indication in the publicly released evidence that Michael or Mary had engaged in an extended physical struggle with their killer.

passages.text: Officers entered the residence. Mary Short was found dead in her bed. She also had been shot once in the head.

passages.text: Investigators described the shootings as execution-style killings.

passages.text: Henry County Sheriff’s Office deputies responded and confirmed that 50-year-old Michael Wayne Short was dead.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities initially considered whether Jennifer could have escaped or hidden during the shootings. After searches around the property failed to locate her, investigators increasingly believed she had been abducted by the person or persons responsible for killing her parents.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Officers and search teams scoured the area surrounding the Short home.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The discovery created two investigations simultaneously:

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer Is Missing: After finding Michael and Mary, officers discovered that their 9-year-old daughter, Jennifer Renee Short, was missing.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael Short had been shot once in the head. A.22-caliber shell casing was recovered near Michael.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Mary Short had been shot once in the head. A second.22-caliber shell casing was recovered near Mary.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The telephone line to the home had been cut.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer was missing.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators began processing the residence for fingerprints, biological material, firearms evidence, and other trace evidence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Crime Scene and Initial Search: Investigators secured the Short property

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators began an intensive search around the residence and the surrounding Henry County area. Investigators searched wooded terrain, roads, structures, and other areas where Jennifer might have gone if she had fled.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Search-and-rescue personnel and volunteers eventually became involved.

passages.text: The investigation rapidly expanded beyond Henry County.

passages.text: Law enforcement also began interviewing:

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: 4:25 p.m. An alert for Jennifer was distributed through the developing AMBER Alert system. Jennifer’s disappearance received widespread regional and eventually national attention.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: According to the October 5 report, Bowman had done odd jobs for Lemons and for Gary Lemons, Lemons’ landlord.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman reportedly worked on mobile homes in the area and was described as a carpenter.

bold: made a telephone call concerning killing a man in Virginia whom he said had failed to pay him for trailer work

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The physical search continued. Investigators worked to reconstruct the Shorts’ movements before the murders and determine who had recently interacted with the family. The working theory remained that Jennifer could still be alive.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman traveled north and ultimately entered Canada.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: His departure would later receive intense scrutiny after Jennifer’s remains were discovered near property associated with him.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: At this point, however, Bowman had not been publicly connected to the Short murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Garrison Bowman Leaves North Carolina: Neighbors later told investigators that Garrison “Gary” Bowman, a 66-year-old carpenter from Rockingham County, North Carolina, left the area on August 16, the day after the Short family crime was discovered.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Lemons said the trailer was essentially empty.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police later searched the residence and found a map of Henry County with a red mark in the area of the Shorts’ home.
bold: a map of Henry County with a red mark in the area of the Shorts’ home

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators also found children’s clothing inside the residence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police seized bedclothes and hair samples from the trailer for examination.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Landlord: Rick Lemons entered the trailer Bowman had rented from him.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Search activity continued. Jennifer’s photographs and home video were distributed publicly to generate sightings.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The investigation received national exposure. Authorities continued emphasizing that they hoped Jennifer remained alive.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: According to the later investigative chronology, this helped investigators focus on Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman’s landlord returned to the residence and spoke with authorities about Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Volunteer searchers continued examining the countryside.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Search dogs were used. Investigators continued receiving and evaluating tips. No confirmed trace of Jennifer was found.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities continued expanding the geographical search. Investigators followed leads in surrounding jurisdictions. No suspect had been identified publicly.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Two.22-caliber shell casings found near Michael and Mary’s bodies and several weapons.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police were searching for a red or dark-colored truck seen leaving the home on the morning of the murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police believed the murderer knew the family.

passages.text: Police filed results of the search of the Short home. 64 items were removed, including

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer’s Belongings and Possible Winston-Salem Sightings: Investigators obtained another search warrant for the Short residence. Investigators sought items that could help establish what Jennifer had with her when she disappeared.
bold: Jennifer’s Belongings and Possible Winston-Salem Sightings:

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Among the property investigators were reportedly interested in were recently purchased school supplies and children’s clothing.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Determining whether specific clothing or belongings were missing could help establish what Jennifer may have been wearing or whether someone deliberately took possessions with her.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Two sightings in the Winston-Salem, North Carolina area received significant investigative attention.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: One witness reported seeing a girl believed to resemble Jennifer in or around a dark-colored truck. The witness reported that the adult male associated with the vehicle displayed or pointed a firearm.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Another witness later reported seeing a girl resembling Jennifer with an adult male near a convenience store.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Law enforcement investigated both sightings. Neither sighting was ultimately confirmed as Jennifer.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Because Jennifer’s remains were later recovered in North Carolina, these reports remained notable but have never been publicly established as genuine sightings of her.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Ruby Young read a statement on behalf of the family pleading directly with the person or persons responsible: “Please release her so she can come home.”
bold: “Please release her so she can come home.”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The family said they missed and loved Jennifer and asked that she not be harmed and be returned safely.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The family also urged anyone with information about Jennifer’s location to contact authorities.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The appearance marked the first time members of the Short family had spoken publicly since Michael and Mary were found murdered and Jennifer disappeared on August 15.
bold: first time members of the Short family had spoken publicly since Michael and Mary were found murdered and Jennifer disappeared on August 15

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Ruby and Chris Young were joined by other relatives, including Carol Whitehead, another sister of Mary Short, and her husband James Whitehead.
bold: Carol Whitehead, another sister of Mary Short, and her husband James Whitehead

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Henry County Sheriff Frank Cassell said investigators had reported no breaks in either Jennifer’s abduction or the murders of Michael and Mary.
bold: no breaks in either Jennifer’s abduction or the murders of Michael and Mary

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Cassell said investigators were continuing to pursue leads, most of them in or near Henry County.

passages.text: Search of Jennifer’s Recovery Site: Investigators returned to the area in Rockingham County, North Carolina, where Jennifer Short’s remains had been discovered and conducted an intensive search for additional evidence.
bold: Rockingham County, North Carolina, where Jennifer Short’s remains had been discovered

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: One year after Michael and Mary Short were murdered and 9-year-old Jennifer Short was abducted, authorities reported no arrests and no suspects.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: A multiagency task force of investigators from the Henry County Sheriff’s Office, Rockingham County authorities, Virginia State Police, and the FBI continued pursuing leads.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Gary Storm Bowman, 67, remained a person of interest. Bowman, a retired carpenter from Mayodan, North Carolina, had left for Canada the day after Michael and Mary’s bodies were discovered.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman had previously worked for Michael Short, complicating investigators’ efforts to evaluate any potential DNA evidence associated with him.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: In the preceding month, Rockingham County investigators obtained DNA samples from Bowman and John Beasley of Stoneville, North Carolina, another acquaintance of Bowman. Authorities sought to determine whether biological evidence linked to the Short investigation could be tied to either man.
bold: DNA samples from Bowman and John Beasley of Stoneville, North Carolina

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators acknowledged that Bowman having DNA at locations associated with Michael Short would not necessarily establish involvement because of his previous association with Michael.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators had also recently searched and dragged a creek near Stoneville that passed beneath the bridge where Jennifer’s remains were discovered, spending several days sifting through the creek. Authorities did not disclose what they were searching for or whether they recovered anything.
bold: searched and dragged a creek near Stoneville that passed beneath the bridge where Jennifer’s remains were discovered

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sheriff Frank Cassell said investigators continued submitting evidence for forensic examination but acknowledged that the perpetrator appeared to have left very little useful physical evidence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Michael Short’s uncle, former Martinsville Police Chief Frank Arrington, publicly questioned whether the number of people allowed around the crime scene may have compromised important evidence. Cassell disputed that characterization.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators continued appealing for information and maintained a reward for information leading to a conviction.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Officials waived the normal 30-day public-comment period after receiving resolutions and letters supporting the memorial designation from Rockingham County officials, sheriffs in Virginia and North Carolina, and U.S. Rep. Virgil Goode.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer Renee Short Memorial Bridge: The North Carolina Highway Department approved naming the bridge on Grogan Road in Rockingham County, North Carolina, near where Jennifer Short’s remains were recovered, the Jennifer Renee Short Memorial Bridge.
bold: Grogan Road in Rockingham County, North Carolina

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The bridge later became a focal point for memorial events honoring Jennifer and her parents.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The annual Jennifer Short Memorial Scholarship Ride, organized for many years by former Short family neighbor Ray Reynolds, traveled from Henry County to the memorial bridge. The event raised tens of thousands of dollars for scholarships for Bassett High School students. The Virginia General Assembly later formally recognized Reynolds for his work.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The memorial designation remains in use. Current NCDOT project documentation specifically identifies the structure as the “Jennifer Renee Short Memorial Bridge” and requires the memorial sign to be reinstalled when the structure is replaced.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities did not publicly explain the specific forensic testing or disclose whether they recovered additional evidence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer’s remains were reburied the following morning.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The procedure followed the earlier exhumation of her father, Michael Short, whose remains had been exhumed in September 2002 for additional forensic examination.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer Short’s Remains Exhumed: Authorities exhumed Jennifer Renee Short’s remains for what investigators described as “forensic purposes.”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators Travel to British Columbia: Investigators traveled to Kamloops, British Columbia, Canada, while pursuing another lead in the Short family murder investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: American investigators met with Canadian authorities at an airfield in Kamloops while attempting to reconstruct the movements and contacts of a person of interest.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The investigation centered on identifying a mystery woman who had reportedly met with a person of interest at the airfield.
bold: mystery woman who had reportedly met with a person of interest at the airfield

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Royal Canadian Mounted Police Cpl. Joanne Skrine confirmed that investigators were examining a meeting between the unidentified woman and a person of interest and attempting to establish the circumstances and timing of their contact.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The unidentified woman was described as a slim Caucasian woman in her late 40s or early 50s with reddish-blonde hair.
bold: slim Caucasian woman in her late 40s or early 50s with reddish-blonde hair

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities believed she might possess information relevant to the Short investigation and sought to identify and interview her.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators did not publicly disclose the identity of the person of interest associated with the meeting.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Forensic Testing: Investigators received results from extensive forensic testing conducted on evidence from the Short investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sheriff Cassell indicated that the results did not provide a definitive forensic breakthrough or “smoking gun.” Investigators nevertheless believed parts of the testing could help the ongoing investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman remained one of the people investigators had examined closely, but no charges followed.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: U.S. Attorney John Brownlee announced that three men faced federal charges for lying to investigators about the Short case.
bold: three men faced federal charges for lying to investigators about the Short case

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sampson had first contacted the Rockingham County Sheriff’s Office on August 15, 2003, exactly one year after the murders, claiming that he had witnessed the crimes.
bold: Rockingham County Sheriff’s Office on August 15, 2003

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sampson claimed that he had been near the Short residence during the early morning hours of August 15, 2002, heard gunshots, and heard a child saying “No, no.”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: He claimed that he saw a man emerge from the Short residence with a weapon and then return outside carrying a child.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sampson later testified before a federal grand jury that the man resembled Abraham Lincoln and eventually connected the name Bowman to the person he claimed to have seen. This was significant because investigators had already identified Garrison Bowman as a person of interest, and Bowman had been described as having a beard and resembling Lincoln.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sampson subsequently recruited Jerry Riley Mills to support his fabricated account. According to the federal court record, Sampson drove Mills to Henry County, showed him the Short murder scene, and rehearsed the false story with him before Mills was interviewed by investigators.
bold: showed him the Short murder scene, and rehearsed the false story with him

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Mills later provided false testimony to the federal grand jury. At Sampson’s subsequent trial, Mills admitted his grand jury testimony was untrue.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sampson also recruited his daughter, Beth Braxton, to provide false corroborating testimony. She initially told the grand jury that Sampson had returned home on the morning of the murders crying and shaking and saying that he had witnessed someone being killed. Braxton later recanted that testimony and testified that she had said what Sampson instructed her to say.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sampson also attempted to recruit Michael Holland to falsely tell FBI investigators that he had sold Mills a Ford van and later had the vehicle crushed. Holland initially repeated the story but quickly contacted investigators and admitted that he had been instructed to lie.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sampson subsequently made threatening telephone calls to investigators, including Rockingham County Sheriff’s Capt. Bobby Lawson and Henry County Sheriff’s Maj. Kimmi Nester. The threats later contributed to a federal sentencing enhancement for obstruction of justice.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators testified that Sampson’s fabricated claims caused law enforcement to expend as many as 1,000 additional investigative hours pursuing false information in the Short case.
bold: as many as 1,000 additional investigative hours

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: False Information and Perjury Charges: Federal prosecutors announced charges stemming from false information provided during the Short family murder investigation. Timothy Fennon Sampson and Jerry Riley Mills were charged in an eight-count federal indictment with offenses including conspiracy, perjury and providing false information to investigators.
bold: Timothy Fennon Sampson and Jerry Riley Mills

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Epperson had approached investigators with information concerning the homicides.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: U.S. Attorney John L. Brownlee personally participated in an interview with Epperson that lasted about five or six hours. Prosecutors ultimately concluded that Epperson’s account was false.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: According to Brownlee, Epperson subsequently acknowledged that the information he provided was false.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Tony Lee Epperson Charged: Federal prosecutors separately charged Tony Lee Epperson with providing false information during the Short investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: A federal grand jury indicted Henry County Sheriff H. Franklin “Frank” Cassell and 19 other defendants in a sweeping federal corruption investigation. Thirteen of the 20 defendants were current or former members of the Henry County Sheriff’s Office, the agency that had led the investigation into the 2002 murders of Michael and Mary Short and the abduction and murder of Jennifer Short.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The 48-count federal indictment alleged offenses including racketeering, illegal narcotics trafficking, theft of firearms, possession of stolen firearms, money laundering, false statements, perjury and obstruction of justice. Federal prosecutors alleged that, beginning as early as 1998, members and associates of the Sheriff’s Office participated in a scheme involving drugs, firearms and other contraband taken from seized evidence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Federal authorities publicly announced the indictments and arrests. Prosecutors alleged that drugs and firearms seized by the Henry County Sheriff’s Office had been stolen and returned to the community for distribution or personal use. Cassell was accused of impeding the federal investigation, making false statements, and helping conceal illegal activity.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Following the arrests, Virginia State Police assisted with law-enforcement operations in Henry County. Cassell subsequently left office, and Capt. Lane Perry was appointed acting sheriff in November 2006.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman No Longer the Primary Focus: Five years after the murders, authorities publicly acknowledged that the investigation of Bowman had not produced evidence sufficient to prosecute him.
bold: Bowman No Longer the Primary Focus

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators increasingly emphasized that the case could not remain centered exclusively on Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman continued to deny killing Michael, Mary or Jennifer. He was never charged with any of the three murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The later discovery that some information pointing investigators toward him had been fabricated further weakened the theory that he was responsible.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Cassell ultimately pleaded guilty to lying to federal investigators. Prosecutors agreed to dismiss the remaining charges against him.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Ultimately, 18 of the 20 defendants entered plea agreements acknowledging involvement in criminal activity, according to Henry County’s own financial records.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The appellate decision documented in detail how Sampson manufactured his account, recruited other people to corroborate it, threatened investigators, and diverted substantial investigative resources from the Short homicide investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit affirmed Sampson’s sentence.
bold: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit affirmed Sampson’s sentence

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Nearly five years after Michael, Mary and Jennifer Short were killed, investigators said they still had no suspects in the case, although several persons of interest remained under investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: FBI Assistant Special Agent in Charge Robert Gwaltney, of the FBI’s Richmond Division, said investigators were “fairly certain” Gary Bowman was not connected to the case.
bold: “fairly certain” Gary Bowman was not connected to the case

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities said Bowman, who had been identified as a person of interest early in the investigation, was no longer a suspect.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators planned to conduct a complete review of all evidence in the case.
bold: complete review of all evidence in the case

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Henry County Sheriff’s Capt. Kimmy Nester said investigators continued to meet every week to discuss the case and follow up on information.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Nester said the investigation had generated “several substantial leads,” but authorities had not been able to develop enough evidence to solve the murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: According to Nester, investigators had made progress in determining who was not responsible, even though they had not determined who was.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Nester said investigators had “put our armor on and keep trucking” and would continue working the case.
bold: “put our armor on and keep trucking”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Jennifer Renee Short Homicide/Abduction Task Force remained active.
bold: Jennifer Renee Short Homicide/Abduction Task Force

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The FBI planned to launch a new website seeking information and accept telephone tips.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: FBI Special Agent Mark MacKizer said investigators had identified individuals of interest and still had specific questions they wanted answered.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators were also looking for people who had never been interviewed, including people who may have considered their information insignificant.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: MacKizer said investigators had identified individuals of interest and had pieces of the puzzle, but did not yet have the complete picture.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The task force was specifically looking for new people to provide information, particularly people who may have withheld information previously because they were afraid, reluctant, or believed what they knew was insignificant.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators planned to approach national television programs to generate additional leads.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Mark MacKizer, an FBI special agent, said the investigators were approaching the case as a new investigation rather than simply reviewing old theories.
bold: new investigation rather than simply reviewing old theories

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The FBI’s Richmond office planned to host a new website dedicated to the Short investigation, allowing investigators to request information about particular aspects of the case and seek specific tips from the public. | Archive
bold: new website dedicated to the Short investigation

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators said the website would allow them to change their requests as the investigation developed, rather than relying only on a general request for information.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: MacKizer said the task force was examining people rather than theories, explaining that investigators were looking at individuals who might fit into different pieces of the investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Spence, who had been involved from the beginning, said the case had been frustrating because investigators had pursued many promising leads that ultimately failed to solve it.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators involved from the beginning were encouraged to step away temporarily, allowing those less familiar with the case to examine it without the assumptions that can develop during a long investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: MacKizer described the approach as essentially starting over, saying investigators would “go back to the beginning” and examine the case again.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The task force intended to revisit witnesses, evidence, investigative leads and potential persons of interest while looking for connections that may previously have been overlooked.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigation has identified a possible vehicle associated with this crime. Information is being sought to further identify this vehicle.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities are seeking information about an unidentified man seen in a car near the Short home on the morning in 2002 when the couple was slain, and their daughter was abducted.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: An update posted on the FBI Web site on Friday was the first revelation that a man had been seen sitting in a car along U.S. 220 in Oak Level near the Shorts’ home early on the morning of Aug. 15, 2002.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The FBI released composite sketches connected to the Short family murder investigation in an effort to identify a man and vehicle reportedly seen near the family’s home on the morning Michael and Mary Short were discovered murdered and Jennifer was found missing.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Despite releasing the composites to the public, authorities could not identify the man or locate the truck.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The man’s presence near the Short residence during the critical morning of the murders made the sighting an important investigative lead. Authorities have not publicly established that the unidentified man was involved in the murders.

passages.text: The FBI released the composite drawing of the unidentified man seen near the Short family’s Oak Level home.

passages.text: The FBI released additional composite information, including an age-progressed depiction of the unidentified man, showing how he might have appeared approximately seven years after the August 2002 sighting. Investigators continued seeking information identifying the man and vehicle.

passages.text: South Carolina Investigation: Authorities announced that members of the Jennifer Renee Short Homicide/Abduction Task Force would travel to South Carolina.

passages.text: Investigators had learned that before his death, Michael Short had made multiple trips to South Carolina while considering a possible family relocation. Michael had been exploring employment opportunities.

passages.text: Authorities wanted to know whether a business interaction, employment contact, dispute or other relationship formed during those trips could explain what happened several months later.

passages.text: The South Carolina investigation did not publicly produce an arrest.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Reward Increase: Investigators temporarily increased the reward for information leading to the arrest of the Short family killers to $100,000. Authorities said the increase was intended to persuade someone with critical information to finally speak with investigators.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators Reexamine Whether Jennifer Was the Intended Target: Thirteen years after Michael, Mary and Jennifer Short were killed, the Henry County Sheriff’s Office began taking a closer look at whether 9-year-old Jennifer, rather than either of her parents, may have been the intended target of the crime.
bold: Investigators Reexamine Whether Jennifer Was the Intended Target:
9-year-old Jennifer, rather than either of her parents, may have been the intended target of the crime

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Henry County Sheriff Lane Perry said investigators were considering whether someone may have specifically targeted Jennifer and killed Michael and Mary because they were present.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Perry explained: “We were thinking, is there a group out there that we haven’t reached out to?”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: He said investigators had previously focused heavily on whether Michael or Mary Short had been targeted, but the passage of time prompted investigators to examine the case from another direction.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Perry said investigators were now asking themselves whether “the thought occurred to us that if Jennifer were alive, she would be college-aged now.”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: That realization led investigators to identify and contact Jennifer’s childhood friends, many of whom were now adults.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators wanted to know whether Jennifer had ever told her friends about anything unusual, frightening or suspicious before she disappeared.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer’s Childhood Friends and Coaches Asked for Help: Henry County investigators publicly appealed to Jennifer’s childhood friends and sports coaches for information.
bold: Jennifer’s Childhood Friends and Coaches Asked for Help:
Jennifer’s childhood friends and sports coaches

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators asked people who knew Jennifer to think back to the period before August 15, 2002 and consider whether Jennifer had ever said anything that seemed unusual or concerning.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sheriff Lane Perry explained that investigators wanted people to ask themselves: “Did Jennifer ever say anything to them? Did they ever have unwanted attention? Did they ever observe anything suspicious?”
bold: “Did Jennifer ever say anything to them? Did they ever have unwanted attention? Did they ever observe anything suspicious?”

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Perry said Jennifer had been active in sports, which prompted investigators to seek information not only from former classmates and friends but also from people who had coached her.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators were particularly interested in whether Jennifer had ever mentioned unwanted attention or whether anyone around her had noticed suspicious behavior involving her.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Perry also said investigators were asking Jennifer’s former friends to remember whether they had similar complaints from their own parents, potentially helping investigators identify a person who had behaved suspiciously around multiple children.
bold: similar complaints from their own parents

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: No arrests had been made in the murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: On the 14th anniversary of the Short family murders, the Henry County Sheriff’s Office renewed its public appeal for information concerning the unsolved killings of Michael, Mary and Jennifer Short.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Sheriff’s Office released a case flyer identifying all three members of the Short family as murder victims and summarized the investigation:

events.title: Family background and early life
events.summary: Michael and Mary's backgrounds, how they met and settled in Henry County, Michael's work, and Jennifer's birth.

events.title: Mary harassed at Pluma plant in 1992
events.summary: An unidentified man repeatedly came to the Pluma plant looking for Mary and left in a white pickup truck; investigators later used old photos of Mary to identify him.

events.title: Family business and South Carolina trips
events.summary: The Shorts ran M.S. Mobile Home Movers Inc., and in 2002 Michael travelled to South Carolina while the family considered moving there; investigators later returned to the area.

events.title: Family life and Jennifer's routine in 2001 and 2002
events.summary: Sheila Davis describes the Shorts as close and hardworking, and Jennifer's summer routine before fourth grade at Figsboro Elementary.

events.title: Plans to sell the house and move
events.summary: In August 2002 the Shorts moved to sell their Henry County home, with an open house scheduled for August 18.

events.title: Bowman's remarks to Rick Lemons
events.summary: Landlord Rick Lemons told investigators that Garrison Bowman was angry about a man who owed him money, said he would have to kill him, and left the area soon after the murders.

events.title: Circle C surveillance footage of Jennifer
events.summary: Surveillance footage at the Circle C convenience store on August 13 shows Jennifer, one of the last known images of her.

events.title: Last known evening at the Short home
events.summary: Chris Thompson stayed near the Short home and worked on a vehicle with Michael on August 14; the family was seen at a Burger King drive-through and a Walmart receipt was recovered.

events.title: Last evening in the living room [for demo purposes]
events.summary: Everything in this file was written by hand to show how the 3D scenes connect to the case graph. None of it comes from the case file. The bedroom is a staged forensic room (Galanakis 2021) and the living room is an office sunroom (Aria Scenes); neither is the Short residence.

events.title: Murders and abduction at the Short home
events.summary: Between midnight and about 9:00 a.m. on August 15, 2002, someone entered the home, cut the phone line, shot Michael and Mary in the head, and took Jennifer.

events.title: Murders discovered and Jennifer reported missing
events.summary: Deputies confirmed Michael Short was dead, Mary and Michael were both shot in the head, two .22-caliber casings were recovered, and Jennifer was missing and believed abducted.

events.title: Initial search and evidence processing
events.summary: Investigators processed the house for evidence, searched the surrounding area, interviewed employees and other groups, and sent an AMBER Alert for Jennifer.

events.title: Bowman's connections and departure
events.summary: Garrison Bowman, a carpenter, had done odd jobs for the Lemons and was linked to a call about killing a man in Virginia; he left North Carolina for Canada on August 16, and police searched his trailer.

events.title: Victims found in the Short home
events.summary: Michael and Mary Short were found with single gunshot wounds to the head, .22-caliber casings were near them, and the home telephone line had been cut.

events.title: Evidence removed and collected from the residence
events.summary: Investigators searched the Short residence at 10680 Virginia Avenue, removed dozens of items, recovered casings and bedding, and ran gunshot residue tests.

events.title: Physical evidence collected from Short residence
events.summary: Investigators collected stains, firearms, bedding, clothing and personal items from the house and Jennifer Short's room.

events.title: Garage and telephone-line evidence
events.summary: Items were collected from the garage and the cut telephone line, and a cellular phone was recovered from a shed.

events.title: Receipts, cash and kitchen items collected
events.summary: Receipts, cash, keys and kitchen items were recovered from the residence.

events.title: Business records seized
events.summary: Investigators removed records from Michael Short's mobile-home moving business.

events.title: Additional evidence collected from residence
events.summary: Investigators collected film, carpet, hairbrushes, a notebook, mail and a central air unit from the residence.

events.title: Forensic reexamination of 2002 evidence
events.summary: Evidence from 2002 was reexamined with advanced DNA testing.

events.title: 3D scene linked to the case [for demo purposes]
events.summary: Everything in this file was written by hand to show how the 3D scenes connect to the case graph. None of it comes from the case file. The bedroom is a staged forensic room (Galanakis 2021) and the living room is an office sunroom (Aria Scenes); neither is the Short residence.

events.title: Living room scene linked to the case [for demo purposes]
events.summary: Everything in this file was written by hand to show how the 3D scenes connect to the case graph. None of it comes from the case file. The bedroom is a staged forensic room (Galanakis 2021) and the living room is an office sunroom (Aria Scenes); neither is the Short residence.

events.title: Search expands and Bowman's landlord speaks
events.summary: Jennifer's photos and home video were released, volunteers searched the countryside, and the landlord told authorities about Garrison Bowman, who became a focus of the investigation.

events.title: Evidence, truck and Winston-Salem sightings
events.summary: Police looked for a red or dark truck seen leaving the home, removed 64 items from the house on a new warrant, and investigated two Winston-Salem sightings that were never confirmed.

events.title: Family public appeals and visitation
events.summary: Relatives publicly pleaded for Jennifer's return on August 21, Sheriff Frank Cassell reported no breaks in the case, and investigators were examining several individuals.

events.title: Investigation of Garrison Bowman begins
events.summary: Investigators received information about Garrison Bowman, searched property tied to him, and obtained warrants based partly on statements from Rick Lemons.

events.title: Human remains found in Rockingham County
events.summary: Remains and a skull were found on the Eddie Albert property on Grogan Road, leading investigators to take a closer look at Garrison Bowman.

events.title: Remains transported for examination
events.summary: The remains were scheduled for transport to the North Carolina state medical examiner's office.

events.title: Autopsy findings on remains
events.summary: The remains were described as a 9-to-10-year-old girl shot in the head, with a skull showing a gunshot wound.

events.title: Searches of Bowman property and recovery sites
events.summary: Investigators searched Bowman's mobile home and North Carolina property, and divers and searchers worked the pond and marshland near the recovery site.

events.title: Garrison Bowman arrested in Canada
events.summary: Canadian police arrested Garrison Bowman in Inuvik on an impaired driving incident, and he was held on an immigration violation while investigators sought to interview him.

events.title: Remains identified as Jennifer Short
events.summary: DNA results positively identified the remains as Jennifer Renee Short, and officials said Michael and Mary Short were her biological parents.

events.title: Remains found near Bowman trailer
events.summary: Jennifer Short's remains were recovered about 1.5 miles from Bowman's trailer, after which police described him as a possible witness.

events.title: Bowman held in Canada on immigration violation
events.summary: Canadian authorities held Garrison Bowman in Yellowknife while he faced deportation and a judge ordered him held longer.

events.title: Investigators travel to Yellowknife to interview Bowman
events.summary: Virginia and North Carolina investigators went to Yellowknife to question Garrison Bowman and seek access to his van, but the interview was delayed by legal authorization issues.

events.title: Jennifer Short funeral and burial
events.summary: The Martinsville Church of God held visitation and funeral services, and Jennifer Short was buried after about six weeks of uncertainty.

events.title: Bowman in Canadian custody and deportation
events.summary: Investigators returned from Canada while Garrison Bowman awaited deportation and planned to question him after his return.

events.title: Investigators collect evidence from Bowman van
events.summary: Investigators returned to Canada to inspect Garrison Bowman's van, collected items, and sent evidence to a Roanoke forensic laboratory, while the van itself stayed in Canada.

events.title: Bowman held as material witness and released
events.summary: Federal authorities detained Garrison Bowman on a material-witness warrant, then released him after prosecutors said he had cooperated.

events.title: Bowman grand jury testimony
events.summary: Garrison Bowman was scheduled to testify before a federal grand jury, continued denying involvement in the Short murders, and was described as a witness of interest.

events.title: Lemons polygraph and grand jury appearances
events.summary: Gary Lemons passed a polygraph confirming his statements about Garrison Bowman, and both Bowman and Lemons appeared before the grand jury.

events.title: Virginia adopts statewide AMBER Alert
events.summary: Virginia adopted a statewide AMBER Alert plan after Jennifer Short's abduction, with Virginia State Police running it.

events.title: Property sold and reward changes
events.summary: The Short home and belongings were sold at auction for the estate, and the reward stood at $42,000 after some donors withdrew.

events.title: Bowman remains a person of interest
events.summary: Investigators said Garrison Bowman was a person of interest, with no evidence tying him to the murders at that point, while a special grand jury investigated the case.

events.title: Creek and recovery-site searches
events.summary: Investigators diverted a creek and searched areas that had been underwater and the recovery site, recovering several articles they declined to identify.

events.title: Bowman still a person of interest one year on
events.summary: A year after the murders no arrests had been made, and Garrison Bowman remained a person of interest who had worked for Michael Short.

events.title: DNA samples and creek search
events.summary: Investigators took DNA samples from Garrison Bowman and John Beasley and searched a creek near Stoneville.

events.title: Memorial bridge naming
events.summary: The North Carolina Highway Department named the Stoneville-area bridge the Jennifer Renee Short Memorial Bridge.

events.title: Exhumations and Jennifer's reburial
events.summary: Authorities exhumed Jennifer Short's remains for forensic purposes and reburied her in late September 2003.

events.title: Kamloops airfield meeting
events.summary: Investigators went to Kamloops, British Columbia, to identify an unidentified woman who had met a person of interest.

events.title: Sampson false witness scheme exposed
events.summary: Federal charges followed the discovery that Timothy Fennon Sampson fabricated a witness account and recruited others to back it.

events.title: Epperson false information charges
events.summary: Tony Lee Epperson approached investigators with information that prosecutors found false, and he was charged.

events.title: Henry County Sheriff's Office corruption indictment
events.summary: A federal grand jury indicted Sheriff Frank Cassell and others over corruption, and Lane Perry became acting sheriff.

events.title: Bowman no longer the primary focus
events.summary: Authorities said the evidence against Garrison Bowman was insufficient and that the case could not focus on him alone.

events.title: Cassell plea and appeal ruling
events.summary: Frank Cassell pleaded guilty to lying to federal investigators and the Fourth Circuit affirmed Sampson's sentence.

events.title: Five-year review finds no suspects and Bowman cleared
events.summary: In 2007 investigators said there were still no suspects, and they told the public Garrison Bowman was no longer a suspect.

events.title: Task force restarts the investigation from the beginning
events.summary: In August 2008 the task force planned new tips and TV outreach and began reviewing the case from the beginning.

events.title: Unidentified man and truck seen near the Short home
events.summary: Investigators learned of a man sitting in a truck near the Short home on the morning of the murders and released composite images of him and the vehicle.

events.title: FBI composites and mobile home movers appeal
events.summary: The FBI released a drawing and an age-progressed image of the unidentified man, and the task force asked people who had homes moved by M.S. Mobile Home Movers to come forward.

events.title: South Carolina trips and 2010 reward increase
events.summary: Investigators examined Michael Short's trips to South Carolina, interviewed people in Bennettsville and Myrtle Beach, and raised the reward to $100,000 without an arrest.

events.title: Jennifer reexamined as possible intended target
events.summary: In 2015 the Henry County Sheriff's Office asked whether Jennifer was the target and sought information from her childhood friends and coaches.

events.title: Anniversary appeal and victim details
events.summary: On the 14th anniversary the Henry County Sheriff's Office renewed its appeal and restated how Michael, Mary and Jennifer Short were killed and where Jennifer was found.

events.title: Former Short home destroyed by fire
events.summary: The former Short residence burned in February 2019, and authorities said it was not connected to the 2002 murders.

events.title: 2021 multi-agency task force review
events.summary: Sheriff Lane Perry assembled a multi-agency task force in 2021 to re-review the case, examine 2002 physical evidence and seek new DNA analysis.

events.title: 2023 Second Fresh-Eyes Task Force
events.summary: Sheriff Wayne Davis authorized a second task force in 2023 that received the full case file to review decades of evidence and reports.

events.title: Second task force progress and DNA testing
events.summary: Sheriff Wayne Davis said the 2023 task force made progress, and old evidence was sent for modern DNA testing by DNA Labs International.

events.title: Current appeal and reward
events.summary: Investigators in 2025 asked for information from people who had contact with the Short family or Michael Short's South Carolina trips, and the reward remained above $60,000.

events.title: Current case status
events.summary: The murders remain unsolved, no one has been charged, and the investigation has broadened beyond Garrison Bowman.

events.title: Case overview and discovery dates
events.summary: The Short victims are listed with their ages, the Henry County location, and the dates Michael and Mary and later Jennifer were found.

events.title: Garrison Bowman becomes a subject of the investigation
events.summary: Investigators searched Garrison Bowman's property and seized maps; he left North Carolina for Canada.

events.title: Garrison Bowman detained and questioned
events.summary: Bowman was held in Canada, detained as a material witness, questioned, and released without charge.

events.title: Bowman legal timeline, 2002
events.summary: Dated sequence of Garrison Bowman's detention, deportation, release and grand jury summons.

events.title: Michael Short's business and South Carolina trips
events.summary: Michael Short operated M.S. Mobile Home Movers and traveled through South Carolina before the murders.

events.title: Modern forensic review of 2002 evidence
events.summary: Task forces and DNA Labs International reexamined preserved evidence from 2002.

events.title: Competing motive theories
events.summary: Investigators have considered whether Jennifer or Michael was the target; none is publicly confirmed.

events.title: Theories about who was targeted
events.summary: Investigators have considered whether the offender targeted the family, Mary Short or Jennifer Short; none is publicly confirmed.

events.title: Victims found and Jennifer removed
events.summary: The telephone line was cut, Michael Short was found in the garage, Mary Short was in her bedroom, and Jennifer Short was removed and later found in rural North Carolina.

events.title: Rick Lemons account about Bowman
events.summary: Rick Lemons reported remarks attributed to Garrison Bowman; later, Timothy Fennon Sampson gave information that led to federal false-statement charges.

events.title: Current status of the case
events.summary: The case remains active; a Henry County investigator, state police and FBI continue work, and 2002 evidence has been retested.
